To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there are 6 main clusters of countries; (2) the number of countries in each cluster has changed little over the past 20 years, but the countries themselves have changed considerably; (3) the number of clusters has increased from 6 to 8; (4) the number of ‘developing countries’ has increased from 104 to 118, but the number of ‘least developed countries’ has decreased from 49 to 34.

the developing world has become more diverse, more unequal, and more dynamic since the late 1980s, and that this has been driven by a number of countries that are not only growing rapidly, but also improving in all dimensions.

• the developing world has changed since the late 1980s in terms both of the country groupings and of the country clusters; • the developing world is still dominated by low-income countries, but it is now much more diverse; • the developing countries are now more heterogeneous in terms of economic development, human well-being, governance, and environmental quality; and • the developing countries have improved their performance in all dimensions of development, but there is still a long way to go.
